vboot: Add init function list INIT_FUNC handlers (including board_setup) are run before vboot is initialized, as they may be preparing interfaces for vboot to use. This means that the board_setup function can't rely on things like vboot_in_recovery() or access to the GBB flags, as these are not available until vboot setup has been run. In order to support this add a list of vboot init functions to be executed before passing control to vboot. This provides a path for board_setup to register a function to be called before vboot is executed to boot a kernel. BUG=b:67029862 BRANCH=eve TEST=manual: boot on Eve with subsequent commit that checks both GBB flags and vboot_in_recovery(). Change-Id: I8bda1de1d1a4fe86a3321ee56f48ec82538ed069 Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/947212 Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org>

eve: Implement workaround for audio The rt5514 codec is getting into a bad state occasionally, and it cannot be revived with normal reboot methods because the codec is on 1.8V DSW power rail which does not drop. This patch implements a workaround in which we attempt to probe the codec at boot and issue a reset via cr50 if it is in a bad state. A byte of unused CMOS is used to ensure the workaround is only attempted once and the system does not get stuck in a reboot loop. The workaround is also not attempted in recovery mode and if GBB flags are set for FAFT testing. This workaround is done in a vboot_init_func callback since the function needs to use both vboot_in_recovery() as well as check GBB flags, and both of those cannot be done at the INIT_FUNC stage as vboot has not been initialized yet. BUG=b:67029862 BRANCH=eve TEST=manual cold reset testing on 6x Eve units, two of which can reproduce this failure regularly. Ensure that the bus is recovered every time and that audio is always functional in the OS. Original-change-id: I17cf0167610e3f402432be9daac3139df368ff34 Original-signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Original-reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/754914 Original-reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Change-Id: I839310b930ecd82b103ae5f4886f0bb5de9e46aa Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/947213 Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>

nvme: Send shutdown command before reboot/poweroff Add support for sending a shutdown command to the NVMe device on a reboot or poweroff cleanup path. The function will try to send a 'normal' shutdown and wait for it to complete, but if that times out it will send an 'abrupt' notification and return immediately. This is only done on devices that have been enabled, that is if the reboot happens before depthcharge touches the device it will not be sent. With my testing this is ok, I did not see an increase in the 'unsafe sutdowns' counter if the device had not been touched by the boot process. BUG=b:73782738 BRANCH=eve TEST=check depthcharge initiated reboots before and after storage has been initialized, in the latter case ensure that the shutdown command is sent and succeeds and that the 'unsafe shutdowns' counter does not increase. Change-Id: I27fa23366aa35ebb8d5807ec02567fcde93b0064 Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/959661 Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>

Adds the following to failed transaction log and kernel messages: return_error : value returned for transaction return_error_param : errno returned by binder allocator return_error_line : line number where error detected Also, return BR_DEAD_REPLY if an allocation error indicates a dead proc (-ESRCH) Bug: 36406078 BUG=None TEST=None Change-Id: Ifc8881fa5adfcced3f2d67f9030fbd3efa3e2cab Test: tested manually Signed-off-by: Todd Kjos <tkjos@google.com> (cherry picked from commit 4cbb47c4d7b3fc270b150df57eed32b931d6d660) Signed-off-by: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/958498 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

ANDROID: FROMLIST: binder: refactor queue management in binder_thread_read (from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9817757/) In binder_thread_read, the BINDER_WORK_NODE command is used to communicate the references on the node to userspace. It can take a couple of iterations in the loop to construct the list of commands for user space. When locking is added, the lock would need to be release on each iteration which means the state could change. The work item is not dequeued during this process which prevents a simpler queue management that can just dequeue up front and handle the work item. Fixed by changing the BINDER_WORK_NODE algorithm in binder_thread_read to determine which commands to send to userspace atomically in 1 pass so it stays consistent with the kernel view. The work item is now dequeued immediately since only 1 pass is needed. BUG=None TEST=None Change-Id: I9b4109997b2d53ba661867b14d7336cd076be06d Signed-off-by: Todd Kjos <tkjos@google.com> (cherry picked from commit 0dc75d4e1d5977585299499640d2098c9f778a0e) Signed-off-by: Prashant Malani <pmalani@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/958499 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

cr50: use system_rollback_detected to detect rollback system_rollback_detected is used to determine if the system rolledback in the rest of the system code base and it's state is saved longer. This change switches board.c to use that to determine the sysinfo output instead of using the reset count. The reset count is cleared when the system boots. Depending on how fast the system boots it may be difficult to read sysinfo before the reset counter is cleared. In these cases it is difficult to tell whether an image has been rejected entirely or the image caused a rollback. BUG=b:71804463 BRANCH=cr50 TEST=boot the device. Make sure sysinfo shows there's no rollback. Rollback and make sure sysinfo shows the system has rolledback Change-Id: Ic29b105c758d0984e47482b9384cf00fe202b716 Signed-off-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/984393 Commit-Ready: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: hugetlbfs: check for pgoff value overflow A vma with vm_pgoff large enough to overflow a loff_t type when converted to a byte offset can be passed via the remap_file_pages system call. The hugetlbfs mmap routine uses the byte offset to calculate reservations and file size. A sequence such as: mmap(0x20a00000, 0x600000, 0, 0x66033, -1, 0); remap_file_pages(0x20a00000, 0x600000, 0, 0x20000000000000, 0); will result in the following when task exits/file closed, kernel BUG at mm/hugetlb.c:749! Call Trace: hugetlbfs_evict_inode+0x2f/0x40 evict+0xcb/0x190 __dentry_kill+0xcb/0x150 __fput+0x164/0x1e0 task_work_run+0x84/0xa0 exit_to_usermode_loop+0x7d/0x80 do_syscall_64+0x18b/0x190 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x3d/0xa2 The overflowed pgoff value causes hugetlbfs to try to set up a mapping with a negative range (end < start) that leaves invalid state which causes the BUG. The previous overflow fix to this code was incomplete and did not take the remap_file_pages system call into account.
